newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine govt says 27 pct workers observed strike.
newsitem.headline: Argentine govt says 27 pct workers observed strike.

text.p: The Argentine government said 27 percent of workers nationwide had observed Thursday's strike by opposition trade unions in protest at unemployment and labor law reform plans.

Interior Minister Carlos Corach called a news conference to give the government's estimate and to disqualify the day's industrial action as "the least successful but most violent" of recent strikes against Peronist President Carlos Menem.

There have been four strikes in little over a year against the jobless rate, now 16.1 percent, and Menem's plans for more modern labor legislation designed to make it easier for companies to hire and fire.

But Thursday's stoppage was opposed by the biggest trade union federation, the CGT, which has signed a deal with Menem for watered-down labor reforms. The strike was called by the smaller MTA and public sector CTA hardline union movements.

CTA leader Victor De Gennaro told Reuters he believed well over half the country's workers had observed the strike, which he called a "rehearsal for the slap in the face" for Peronism in mid-term elections for Congress due in October.
Corach said there were 270 incidents of violence up and down the country and 95 people arrested in the populous Buenos Aires Province.

But there were no major marches or demonstrations and the incidents were limited to roadblocks in outlying provinces, isolated fire attacks on strike-breaking buses and clashes between police and roadblockers on the outskirts of Buenos Aires, where six people were hurt and two arrested.
The center of the capital was calm with shops and offices open for business as usual.
